text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm sketching a small rubric for LLM-as-judge that we'll use for onboarding new models. Need input on bias checks and tie-breaker logic. rough goals: 1) reproducible verdicts, 2) low judge cost, 3) graceful handling of ties / low-confidence.
neal: +1 on reproducibility. we should pin seed + model-version for judges in CI runs. also record logits when available for confidence. :thumbsup:
samir: For bias checks, can we include a small demographic slice set (gender/age/geo) and report per-slice disagreement rate? If judges disagree more on certain slices that's a red flag.
jen: Agree. Also we hit flakiness last week when the judge model got quantized variant in the runner. CI used judge:v1-quant, but evals assumed float — mismatch caused inconsistent scores. We need explicit judge model mapping in the harness.
maria: Good catch. Proposal: harness config fields judge_model_id, judge_quantized (bool), seed. CI job validates that mapping before running.
neal: On tie-breakers: prefer deterministic rules first (higher average score), then if within epsilon use a deterministic tie-breaker prompt with second judge model (cheaper, different architecture) as arbiter. Avoid randomness when possible.
samir: How about consistency checks across judge pool? e.g., run 3 small judges (main + two light) and compute majority vote; if no majority, mark as ambiguous and escalate to human review. That keeps automated decisions conservative.
maria: I like majority + human escalation for ambiguous. But cost: running 3 judges for every sample doubles/triples cost. Maybe run 1 judge by default and only trigger the 3-judges path for samples near the decision boundary (score gap < 0.08).
jen: That conditional path makes sense. Also add a caching layer for judge outputs keyed by (prompt_hash, model_under_test, judge_model_id, seed) to avoid rerunning identical judgments across experiments.
eval-bot: automated note: pilot run 2024-10-15 03:12UTC on dataset "onboard-v2"; 18% of samples fell within gap < 0.08 and would have triggered multi-judge arbitration.
neal: Bias mitigation: we should include a symmetry test — flip names/pronouns in sensitive samples and check variance in judge output. If variance > threshold, flag for manual inspection.
samir: Also track per-judge calibration using Brier score over a held-out human-labeled seed set. If judge calibration drifts, do not use it for automatic pass/fail.
maria: Ops checklist I'm drafting: config pin, seed pin, judge caching, conditional multi-judge arbitration, per-slice bias report, flip-pronoun symmetry test, calibration monitor, human-escalation queue. Can people +1 which items they can own?
neal: I'll take seed pin + CI validation job.
samir: I'll own bias slice definitions + symmetry tests.
jen: I'll do caching + judge model mapping in the runner. Also will add a small CI test that simulates quantized vs float mismatch.
maria: Thanks — I'll wire the escalation queue and update the eval harness README. Will post a PR for the rubric doc by EOD.
eval-bot: reminder: open PRs that touch evaluator runners must include a stable-seed test and a quantized-variant smoke test per the new guidelines.
maria: End — will follow up in the PR thread with sample rubric YAML and example CI job config.
